title: God’s supreme truthfulness is per se known — if perceived as God’s word, absolute certainty follows
source_text: XXII. Jam autem est quidem per se notum Deum esse summe veracem, ac plane fieri non posse ut mentiatur, & falsum testimonium perhibeat. Adeoque si quis certo & evidenter percipiat aliquid a Deo dici & asseri, inde proculdubio in mente ejus formabitur certitudo summa atque absoluta.
pass_a_gloss: But now it is indeed known through itself that God is supremely truthful, and that it plainly cannot be that He lie and bear false testimony. And so if anyone certainly and evidently perceives something to be said and asserted by God, thence without doubt the highest and absolute certainty will be formed in his mind.
pass_b_english: Per se known: God supremely truthful — cannot lie/false-testify.
If something is certainly/evidently perceived as said by God → absolute certainty follows.

choices.term: est quidem per se notum Deum esse summe veracem
choices.english: it is indeed known through itself that God is supremely truthful
choices.why: Grants first condition; pivots to XXIII’s second.
rejected: God’s truthfulness itself needs moral proof first
